name: default
source: docs/00-formula-index.md, cross-checked against the worked calculations in docs/12-quarter-1-reference.md

survival.source: docs/17-designer-resolutions.md — Tier Assignment; cash_exhausted is the unambiguous cash-zero line rather than a stated rule

conditions.rule: at the tier-assignment quarter only: quarter_ncf < 0 AND cash fell 2+ consecutive quarters

scoring.source: docs/10-scoring-methodology.md for the trait weights, sub-criteria text, modifier triggers and bands. The MECHANICAL/JUDGMENT classification and the four unsourced thresholds below are this implementation's own read (docs/19-work-split.md T1), not designer-confirmed.

criteria.description: A stated, coherent thesis exists behind the allocation (not a random or default split)
criteria.reason: 'Stated' asks for the student's own reasoning. QuarterAllocations carries spend numbers, not a rationale field -- there is nothing in the pure engine's output that represents what the student said.

criteria.description: The thesis is genuinely followed through in the actual numbers, not abandoned partway
criteria.reason: Checking follow-through requires knowing what the thesis was (see strategic_thinking_1); with no stated thesis captured, there is nothing to check the numbers against.

criteria.description: The thesis correctly targets wherever the quarter's real constraint actually is (demand, capacity, conversion ceiling, or cash)
criteria.reason: QuarterResult can say which gate bound this quarter (capacity_bound/ceiling_bound/supply_bound), but the criterion asks whether the student's thesis targeted it -- that comparison needs the thesis, which isn't captured.

criteria.description: Decisions are made without excessive hedging or indecision
criteria.reason: Hedging and indecision are properties of how a decision was made, not of the resulting spend numbers -- no field in QuarterResult or QuarterAllocations carries process information.

criteria.description: The student is proactive -- raising issues or opportunities themselves, not only reacting when prompted
criteria.reason: Proactivity is about whether the student raised something unprompted. The engine only sees the final allocation, never whether or how it was prompted.

criteria.description: The student owns the trade-offs their allocation makes, rather than ignoring or downplaying them
criteria.reason: Ownership is expressed in what the student says about their decision, not in the decision's numbers -- nothing here is inferable from spend alone without inventing a proxy.

criteria.description: The student recognises when a prior quarter's approach no longer fits the current situation
criteria.reason: Recognition is a claim about the student's awareness, not a fact derivable from comparing two QuarterResults -- a changed allocation is consistent with recognition, drift, or coincidence alike.

criteria.description: The change made is driven by evidence (results, audits, carryover data), not arbitrary impulse
criteria.reason: Distinguishing evidence-driven from arbitrary change needs the student's stated motivation; the engine has no such field.

criteria.description: The change, once made, is well-executed -- not just attempted
criteria.reason: Identifying 'the change' at all depends on knowing what was attempted and why (adaptability_1/2), which isn't captured, so execution quality against it can't be checked either.

criteria.description: Cross-department dependencies are correctly identified (e.g. leads vs. capacity, conversion vs. quality ceiling, demand vs. supply)
criteria.reason: 'Correctly identified' asks about the student's stated understanding of the dependency, not just its numeric consequence -- the consequence is checkable (systems_thinking_2/3 do), the identification claim is not.

criteria.description: Departments are sized in coordination with each other, not decided in isolation
criteria.reason: Checked from QuarterResult: effective_leads vs. effective_sales_capacity, and total_units_demanded vs. available_to_sell, must each sit within thresholds.coordination_ratio of 1.0 (built to match, not wildly over- or under-sized relative to each other).

criteria.description: No single department is left as an unaddressed bottleneck once the rest of the allocation is finalised
criteria.reason: QuarterResult already reports capacity_bound, ceiling_bound and supply_bound. Zero or one gate binding is coordinated; every additional simultaneous gate is another bottleneck left unaddressed.

criteria.description: A real cash or debt safety margin exists after the allocation is made
criteria.reason: discretionary_ceiling_inr minus total_discretionary_inr on QuarterResult is exactly this margin; spent_into_buffer is the boolean collapse of the same fact.

criteria.description: Downside exposure is bounded, not open-ended, if assumptions prove wrong
criteria.reason: This asks about exposure under hypothetical futures that didn't happen -- QuarterResult only carries what did happen, not what the student's assumptions were or how they'd fail.

criteria.description: The level of risk taken is proportionate to the evidence available at the time of the decision
criteria.reason: Explicitly asks what was known 'at the time of the decision' -- the engine only has the outcome, not a reconstruction of what evidence preceded it.

criteria.description: Marginal spend in each department roughly matches that department's marginal return
criteria.reason: 'Roughly matches' is a comparative judgment across department-specific marginal-return curves; deriving and comparing all of them would be inventing an evaluation formula docs/ does not state.

criteria.description: No channel or department is funded past the point where extra spend stops producing extra usable output (a hard cap, a capacity ceiling, or a demand ceiling)
criteria.reason: Checked from QuarterResult: referral_wasted_spend_inr > 0 means Referral was funded past its hard cap; capacity_bound means Marketing was funded past what Sales Capacity can use.

criteria.description: No channel or department is left funded below the level that proven demand or a known constraint would justify
criteria.reason: Checked from QuarterResult: capacity_bound means Sales Capacity was funded below the demand Marketing proved; supply_bound means Operations was funded below proven demand; ceiling_bound means R&D was funded below what Sales/Marketing's raw conversion could use.

criteria.description: At least one investment is made whose payoff is not this quarter's (e.g. a compounding score, a long-horizon mechanic)
criteria.reason: Checked from QuarterAllocations: any spend on the compounding lines (meta_ads, social_influencer, events_pr, content_seo, prelaunch_buzz, innovation) qualifies -- all build a cumulative score that pays out in a later quarter.

criteria.description: That investment is not sacrificed entirely for short-term gain when the two compete for the same budget
criteria.reason: 'When the two compete' asks about a trade-off the student faced; the engine sees the resulting split, not whether a competing short-term option was passed over for it.

criteria.description: The long-term investment is sized proportionately to the company's current stage and cash position
criteria.reason: 'Current stage' is an interpretive read of where the company is in its trajectory, not a field in CompanyState -- there is no stated formula mapping cash/history to a 'stage'.

standard.rule: the hard-capped Referral channel hit its lead cap exactly: channel_leads['referral'] == referral_lead_cap AND referral_wasted_spend_inr == 0

this quarter's spend on a compounding line (Brand-building: meta_ads+social_influencer+events_pr; SEO: content_seo; Buzz: prelaunch_buzz; Innovation: innovation) is below thresholds.compounding_cut_ratio of that line's prior-quarter spend
standard.note: Needs prior_allocations, not just prior_result -- QuarterResult carries derived leads/scores, not the raw spend figures a fair quarter-over-quarter investment comparison needs. See engines/scoring.py.

standard.rule: a loan or credit line is used without a stated reason tied to a specific, funded growth plan
standard.note: The 22-line chain has no debt/loan mechanic at all -- FIN-005 lives only in the parked legacy percentage-influence pipeline (app/engines/legacy_matrix/). This modifier is configured so its absence is visible rather than silently missing, but engines/scoring.py's predicate always returns 'did not fire'.

crisis.rule: the crisis event's core mechanism (scenario-specific: A/B's conversion penalty, C's Innovation-threshold conversion+ceiling complex, D's Capacity Multiplier) was reduced to zero net effect
crisis.note: docs/14 section 7's own worked scoring table gives Scenario B a 'Partial (+1)' tier that docs/11 (the spec of record) never states a rule for -- this predicate is strictly binary (docs/11's stated definition), so B's expert case returns 'did not fire' rather than a guessed partial-credit amount. A documented, reported residual, not a bug.

crisis.rule: the crisis was substantially handled by investment made before this quarter's crisis-specific response, not by the expensive reactive spend -- scenario-specific signal (Innovation Score for Feature Leapfrog, Supplier Reliability for Supply Shock's Capacity Multiplier >= 0.90); no documented prior-investment-alone path exists for Price Warrior or Marketing Blitz

Choice B on Supply Shock, converting the crisis into a permanent Supplier Reliability gain (docs/14 section 6: +10, forever) -- the only scenario/choice combination with a stated permanent-asset outcome
Rs 0 spent on the relevant response line during a crisis quarter, and the crisis was not otherwise neutralized or proofed by prior investment

raw_conversion_composition.formula: base + Reps bonus + CRM bonus + CX Team repeat-rate bonus + Buzz Q+2 bonus
raw_conversion_composition.note: CX Team's term reproduces both Q2 variants in docs/13 §4/§5, but both used the same Rs 1,50,000 CX spend -- one data point, not a confirmed curve. See docs/10-implementation-gaps.md.

referral.note: No profile-side constants by design. Referral is a hard cap, not a curve: cap ratio and flat cost-per-lead are both company data and live in the seed config.

brand_multiplier.note: Not stated in source. Fitted to 3 data points in docs/13-quarter-2-reference.md §2.1
